back: A disease always present in an area at a steady level (e.g. malaria in some low-lying areas).
A sudden rise in cases of a disease in one community or region, well above normal.
An epidemic that spreads across many countries and continents (e.g. COVID-19).

front: When did Zimbabwe record its first COVID-19 case?
When was Zimbabwe's major cholera outbreak?
How is cholera spread and prevented?
back: Through water or food contaminated with faeces; prevented by safe water, toilets, hand washing and food hygiene.

front: Name three ways HIV is NOT spread.
back: Hugging or shaking hands, sharing plates or cups, mosquito bites.

front: Why does stigma make epidemics worse?
back: People who fear rejection hide symptoms and avoid testing and treatment, so disease spreads.

front: Give one strength and one weakness of COVID-19 lockdowns.
back: Strength: slowed spread. Weakness: informal traders lost income and learners lost schooling.
